fitAnalysis.assessment:
Your fit for this Senior Program Manager role is a WEAK FIT at 18%, so upskilling is recommended first.

**Strengths:**
- Variance analysis and management reporting (Calder Industrial Components)
- Power BI and Excel (VBA) for data-driven performance tracking
- Rolling forecasts and budgeting that support business-case building

**Gaps:**
- 12-15+ years of program management or workplace operations experience (you have about 6 in finance)
- No cross-functional program ownership or global program delivery
- No JIRA or Airtable, workflow automation, or vendor management experience

**Recommendation:** Target finance-adjacent roles, such as FP&A or finance operations, or a junior program or operations role, while you build program management experience and finish your ACCA.

coverLetter:
Tomas Brandt
Chicago, IL, USA
tomas.brandt@example.com
+1 555 0123

October 12, 2026

Hiring Manager
Airbnb

Dear Hiring Manager,

Your Workplace Operations teams each run their own processes, tools and vendors across a global office footprint, and that makes it hard to see where effort is duplicated or where manual work could be automated. I've worked on a version of that problem in finance. Month-end close reporting at Calder Industrial Components took 9 working days, so I automated the journal checks in Excel VBA and cut it to 6.

I'm a Financial Analyst, not a program manager, and I won't pretend otherwise. What I do have is the analytical groundwork your role leans on. I own the monthly forecast and variance reporting for two business units with combined revenue of about 85 million USD. I build Power BI dashboards on SAP data for plant managers, and I rebuilt a forecasting model around order backlog, which raised accuracy for the larger unit from 88% to 96%. That is the habit of measuring performance and building a business case from data that your measurement frameworks and efficiency gains call for. I'm also curious about how emerging technology changes operational work, and I've shown I'll build the tooling myself when a manual process gets in the way.

I'd welcome a conversation about how that analytical and automation mindset could support your Workplace Ops modernization. I'm available to speak at your convenience.

Best regards,
Tomas Brandt
